Chapter 7: Measuring and Monitoring Fairness
Let’s take a closer look at how organizations can really sustain fairness. The secret? You’ve got to measure it—both in numbers and in stories.
Now, don’t worry, this isn’t about boiling down people’s experiences to cold statistics. Think of data more like a flashlight—helping you spot what you might otherwise miss, so you can track how far you’ve come.
Measuring fairness might sound a little abstract at first. But actually, it becomes a lot more manageable when you break it into a few simple steps.
First, there’s collecting data. That means keeping an eye on things like pay equity, promotion rates, turnover, and the makeup of your team. And it’s not just about the numbers—you’ll also want to run regular surveys, asking people how fair, trusted, and included they really feel.
Next, analyze the patterns. Look for any disparities between groups—think gender, race, tenure, or even department. Are some folks leaving more often? Are certain voices missing from the leadership table?
Once you’ve got the insights, it’s time to act. Use what you’ve learned to update policies, shape training, or roll out targeted programs. And here’s a big one—be open with the results. Let everyone know what you found and what you plan to do next.
For example, imagine a company discovers, through exit interviews, that women are leaving more often because they don’t see opportunities to move up. That’s a powerful insight—and it could spark a review of promotion criteria, or the launch of a new mentorship program.
But numbers alone don’t tell the whole story. It’s just as important to check the “temperature” of fairness with things like pulse surveys or honest focus groups. These conversations can reveal how people really feel in the moment—capturing subtle details that data might miss.
Here’s the key takeaway: when organizations keep a regular eye on fairness, they can spot issues early and adapt quickly. This kind of ongoing attention shows employees that fairness isn’t just a one-time thing—it’s something the organization lives and breathes every day.
